La Luna tiene una exosfera extremadament: The Moon has a very thin exosphere: you cannot breathe it or hear sounds through it like on Earth. Mars has a thin atmosphere, mostly carbon dioxide. You need a spacesuit there too.
Usamos referencias gravitacionales aprox: We use approximate gravity values of 1.62 m/s² on the Moon and 3.71 m/s² on Mars. Supplies, speeds, recipes and travel times are simplified game settings.
El cielo es una ilustración pixelada: no: The pixel sky is an illustration, not an astronomy chart or a real camera exposure. The Moon has no atmospheric clouds; Mars has a thin haze.
El mapa y los depósitos minerales o de h: The map, minerals and ice deposits are fictional. They do not recreate a real landing site. Workshop recipes simplify processing iron ore.
El segundo impulso del traje consume ene: The second suit boost uses energy. It is a fictional game ability, not a feature of a NASA spacesuit.
El aviso solar es un ejercicio programad: Solar warnings are scheduled drills, not live DONKI alerts. Exposure is a learning score, not a radiation dose. The shelter reduces risk but is not a certified shielding design. Growing food uses seeds, water and electricity. OSDR plant research supports the need for light and water, not the fast harvest time in this game.
